- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward correction by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), reduce subsequent forecast slope to prevent runaway momentum.  
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.3–0.7), favor mean reversion toward recent 7–14 day average, not long-term trend.  
- If true outcome deviates from forecast by >10% in early period (e.g., day 1–5), adjust model to align with sentiment volatility — higher sentiment = higher early correction.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment shows strong divergence from price trend (e.g., sentiment up but price down), reduce forecast lag by 1–2 days.
